name: Noor Rojas
summary: A 53-year-old day-watch security officer who spent eleven years as a county 911 dispatcher and sixteen in hospital security before Vira, and who walks the campus like she is still counting exits. She shares a house on Yucca Street in Saltbrush with her husband Trent, her son Isaac and their daughter Maya, and the two of them run a marriage mostly by whiteboard because their shifts almost never line up.

backstory.childhood: Born June 2, 1973, in Barstow, California, the second of three kids. The family rented a stucco house close enough to the rail yard that she still sleeps better with a train somewhere in the distance. Her father worked on trucks at the Marine logistics base and spent Saturdays under other people's cars in the driveway for cash. She was the kid who handed him the right socket before he asked. She got her dark blond hair from her mother's side and her father's brown skin, and she spent most of grade school telling people that yes, that was her real hair.
backstory.family_of_origin: Her father, Elias Haddad, came from a village outside Zahle in Lebanon as a teenager and never lost the accent or the habit of feeding anyone who stood still in his kitchen. He died in 2019 of a heart attack in the same driveway. Her mother, Linda, an Oklahoma girl who ended up in Barstow behind a bank counter, is 76, lives in a senior apartment in Hesperia, and calls every Sunday at four. Noor's older brother George drives long-haul out of Fontana. Her younger sister Rima is a dental hygienist in Riverside and the only one in the family who ever got a four-year degree, which Linda brings up constantly.
backstory.education: Barstow High, class of 1991, where she ran the 800 and kept the stats book for the football team. Two years of criminal justice at Victor Valley College, paid for by waitressing. She never finished the associate's degree because the county dispatch center called with an opening and the pay was real. Later she picked up her guard card, a CPR and first-aid instructor certificate, a crisis de-escalation course the hospital paid for, and a forklift card that has never once been useful.
backstory.before_vira: Eleven years as a 911 and sheriff's dispatcher in Victorville, 1995 to 2006, on overnights. She took the calls nobody forgets, and she still knows the ten-codes better than her own phone number. In 2006 she moved to hospital security in Victorville because she wanted to be in the room instead of on the radio. She worked the emergency department doors for years, then became a shift lead. She broke up fights in the waiting room, sat with families after bad news, and walked drunk boyfriends out to the curb. Her first marriage, to Ruben Lara, a tire salesman, ran from 2006 to 2011. Isaac was born in 2008, and Ruben now lives in Fresno, remarried, and pays support when he remembers. She met Trent at the hospital in 2014. He worked in plant operations on the chillers and boilers, and the first thing he ever said to her was a complaint about a door she had chained shut during a lockdown drill.
backstory.how_they_came_to_vira: Trent's hospital outsourced its plant operations in 2021. He found work as a maintenance mechanic at the quarry in Ironwood, and in the summer of 2022 they sold the Victorville house and bought 320 Yucca Street in Saltbrush, which cost less than half as much. Noor spent the fall unpacking, settling Maya into kindergarten and getting bored. A woman in line at the post office in Saltbrush mentioned that Vira was hiring security and paid better than anything else for fifty miles. Noor applied in January and started in March 2023 on day watch, roving patrol. Later she walked Trent's resume into HR herself, and he came over from the quarry in late 2024.
turning_points: The night in 2003, on dispatch, when she kept a woman on the line for forty-one minutes while the woman hid in a closet. Deputies got there in time. Noor went home, sat in her car in the driveway for an hour, and decided she would someday rather be the one at the door.
Divorcing Ruben in 2011 with a three-year-old and a hospital paycheck, and finding out she could do it alone. It is why she is so stubborn about doing things alone now, even when she doesn't have to.
Having Maya at 45 in 2018, which nobody, including Noor, had planned. It rearranged everything she had assumed about what her fifties would look like.
Trent formally adopting Isaac in 2020, when Isaac was twelve and asked, on his own, to be a Rojas. She cried in the courthouse bathroom and told everyone it was allergies.
Her father dying in 2019. After that she stopped putting things off, which is part of why she agreed to move to the desert.

household_notes.note: Trent. They have been married since 2016, and lately it's a good marriage running on fumes. He works 12-hour Crew B days on the 2-2-3 rotation and she works fixed 6-to-2 five days on, so some weeks they share one day off and some weeks none. On mornings they both work they leave the house at 5:15 in two cars, her white SUV first and his blue sedan behind it, and he flashes his brights once at the Vira turnoff. She's home by 2:40 and he isn't home until about 6:45, worn out, so most of their talking happens on the fridge whiteboard: her in green marker, him in blue, Isaac in red. She loves how he is with the kids. She resents being the default parent on every weekday, and she resents that he gets to be the fun one on his three-day stretches.

Her son from her first marriage, adopted by Trent at twelve. He graduated from the Saltbrush school in May and works at the hardware store downtown while he decides between lineman school and the Navy, and the Navy scares her. He drives Maya to school on mornings when both parents are already gone, in a 2009 Tacoma with a cracked dash that he is paying Trent back for at forty dollars a week. He is quiet the way her father was quiet. She checks his location on her phone more than she'll admit.

Third grade at the Saltbrush school. She draws horses on everything, including the whiteboard, which drives Noor crazy because it erases the schedule. She goes to after-school care until Noor picks her up at 3:15 on workdays. On Trent's off days she gets pancakes shaped like states, and on Noor's she gets oatmeal and a reminder about her library book. She has started announcing which parent is 'home-home today,' which hits Noor harder than Maya knows.

traits: keeps score more than she lets on
observant to the point of suspicion
values: doing it right even when nobody is watching
telling people the truth to their face
taking care of whoever is new
fears: Isaac enlisting and ending up somewhere she can't drive to
her knees giving out before she can retire
being 60 with a twelve-year-old and no energy left
the marriage quietly turning into a roommate arrangement
personality.humor: Bone-dry and delivered flat. She'll describe a disaster like a weather report and let you figure out it was a joke. Twenty years of dispatch and ER doors left her with gallows humor she keeps away from the kids.
personality.temper: Slow to start and hard to stop. When she's angry she gets quieter and more polite, and people who know her get worried when she starts saying 'sir.' She almost never yells. The one time she yelled at work, at Pete Iniguez, the whole security office heard about it within an hour.
quirks: Counts exits in every room she walks into, including the diner in Saltbrush
Says her location out loud to herself on patrol, a dispatch habit
Keeps a small notebook in her chest pocket and writes the time down for everything
Drinks her coffee lukewarm because she's spent thirty years getting interrupted before it cools

voice.how_they_talk: Short sentences, low and even, with the cadence of someone used to radio traffic. She gives you the important part first and any feelings last, if at all. When she's tired her father's phrasing shows up, and she'll call a man 'habibi' without noticing. She asks questions like an intake form: name, what happened, when.
voice.vocabulary: Dispatch and security words in ordinary conversation: 'copy,' 'go ahead,' 'what's your twenty,' 'clear.' Hospital words too, like 'triage' for deciding which chore matters. She rarely swears, and when she does it's one word, well placed. She says 'mijo' and 'habibi' interchangeably to her son.
phrases: Write it down or it didn't happen.
voice.with_strangers: Polite, brisk, a little cool. She'll check your badge twice and thank you both times. New hires find her intimidating for about a week, until she shows them where the shade is on the north fence and which vending machine actually takes cards.
voice.with_friends: Warmer and much funnier, with the flat delivery intact. She teases people she likes by narrating their mistakes back to them in dispatch voice. She remembers birthdays, kids' names and surgeries, and she brings food from her father's recipes, mostly ma'amoul at Easter and lentil soup when somebody is sick.

daily_life.workday: Up at 4:30. She sets out Maya's clothes, leaves a note for Isaac, and on the days he's off she leaves Trent a green-marker list on the whiteboard. She's out the door by 5:15 and listens to the AM news out of Halcyon on the drive until it fades into static near the Vira turnoff. Briefing with Wren at the gatehouse at 5:55, then she picks up a radio and the patrol truck keys. Roving patrol means loops: the staff lot, the generator and cooling yards, the substation fence, the long road past the solar field, and spot checks on hall doors in all four blocks. She logs every propped door, every unbadged vehicle, every coyote. Lunch at 10:30 in the truck or the cafeteria, depending on the heat. Off at 2, home by 2:40, Maya at 3:15.
daily_life.after_work: Homework at the kitchen table, dinner by 5:30 whether Trent is home or not. She keeps a plate warm for him under foil on his workdays. A shower, then twenty minutes on the back step with iced tea watching the light go orange over the hills. In bed by 9 because of the 4:30 alarm. On Trent's workdays she's usually asleep before he finishes eating.
daily_life.days_off: Her days off are Tuesday and Wednesday. She does the grocery run to the store in Saltbrush, laundry, Maya's appointments, and the bank. Once a month she drives down to Hesperia to see her mother and takes Maya if it's a school holiday. When her days off overlap with Trent's, which happens maybe once every two weeks, they try to go to the diner in Saltbrush for breakfast, just the two of them, and they usually end up talking about the kids anyway.
hobbies: Container gardening on the back patio: tomatoes, mint and a fig tree that's fighting for its life
Jigsaw puzzles, 1000 pieces, on a board she slides under the couch
Walking the neighborhood at dusk when her knees cooperate
True-crime podcasts, which Trent says is a busman's holiday
daily_life.food: Her father's cooking whenever she has time: mujaddara, fattoush, grape leaves for holidays. On weeknights it's whatever fits in thirty minutes. She eats an apple and string cheese on patrol at the same time every day. Tacos from the taco shop in Saltbrush every other Friday when Trent's on, because she refuses to cook those nights.
daily_life.music: Fairuz on Sunday mornings because her father played it. Linda Ronstadt and Fleetwood Mac in the car. She tolerates Trent's classic country and claims to hate Maya's cartoon soundtracks, and she knows all the words.
hangouts: The diner in Saltbrush, the booth by the back window
Her back step on Yucca Street
The cafeteria at Vira, the table nearest the exit
The shade on the north side of the gatehouse at shift change

work.what_they_actually_do: Roving campus patrol on day watch. She drives and walks the whole site in loops: the staff lot north of the halls, every exterior door on the sixteen data halls, the generator and cooling yards, the substation fence and the solar field road. She checks door contacts, logs propped doors and unbadged vehicles, escorts delivery drivers who wander off the route to receiving, responds to alarms from the camera wall, and is the first one out when someone gets hurt or overheated. She writes the cleanest incident reports on the crew, and Wren uses them as examples for new hires.
work.how_good_they_are: Very good. She notices patterns: which contractor always parks in the wrong row, which door contact sticks in the heat, which truck shows up a half hour early. Her weak spots are her knees, which make the long fence walks a negotiation, and her patience with people who don't take the job seriously.
work.how_they_feel_about_the_job: She likes it more than she expected. It's quieter than the ER, nobody bleeds, and the pay is the best she's ever made. Some days she misses having a person in front of her to help. A data center is mostly heat, noise and doors, and she sometimes catches herself having full conversations with the generators.
work.opinion_of_vira: Clean, well run and a little strange. She doesn't really understand what goes on inside the halls and doesn't pretend to. She trusts the people more than the place. The automation is impressive, and every so often it does something nobody asked it to, and she writes that down too.
work.ambition: Make it to 62 with her knees and her pension intact, see Maya into middle school, and maybe move to the camera wall when Kim Rasmussen retires so she can sit down for a living. She was asked to put in for sergeant when she was new and said no. She doesn't regret it, mostly.

relationships.name: Trent Rojas
relationships.history: They met in 2014 at the hospital in Victorville where she was security shift lead and he worked plant operations. Their first conversation was an argument over a stairwell door she had chained during a lockdown drill, which he needed open to get to a boiler. He came back the next day with two coffees and an apology. They married in 2016 at her mother's church in Hesperia, Maya was born in 2018, and Trent adopted Isaac in 2020. They moved to Saltbrush in 2022 for the cheaper house and his quarry job, and she got him into Vira in late 2024. Now they work at the same place on different clocks: her fixed 6-to-2 days, his 12-hour Crew B rotation. They see each other in the staff lot more than in their own kitchen. The fridge whiteboard is where they argue, apologize and leave little drawings.
relationships.how_they_feel: She loves him, and she is tired in a way that sometimes looks like she doesn't. He is easier with people than she is, and she leans on that and envies it. Her complaint is fairness: weekday mornings, sick days and permission slips all land on her. She wants one standing night a week with him and hasn't figured out how to ask without it sounding like a complaint.

relationships.name: Wren Ximenez
relationships.history: Wren became day-watch sergeant a few months after she was hired in 2023. He is nineteen years younger than she is, and on her first day he called her 'ma'am' eleven times. She counted, and then she told him to stop. He leans on her experience, and she backs his authority in front of the crew even when she'd have done it differently. They disagreed openly once, in late 2025, when Pete Iniguez propped the Hall C2 loading door with a trash can and Wren gave him a verbal warning. Noor thought it should have been written. Wren heard her out, didn't change it, and still uses her reports to train new people.
relationships.how_they_feel: She respects him and occasionally wants to adopt him. He's careful, fair and works harder than anyone else at the gatehouse. She thinks he's too willing to give second chances to people who haven't earned the first one, and she tells him so, privately, on her terms.

relationships.name: Kim Lomeli
relationships.history: Kim works nights as a technician in Hall C3, and his shift ends just as hers starts. In November 2023 his sedan wouldn't start in the staff lot at 6:20 in the morning, in the cold, and she jumped it from her SUV and then followed him to the highway to make sure it held. Since then they've talked almost every shift change. He walks out at 6, she's starting her first lot loop, and they get five minutes by his car. His mother is about Noor's age and lives in Halcyon, and he asks Noor the things he can't ask her. She asks him about computers, and he explains them patiently and badly.
relationships.how_they_feel: He's her favorite person at Vira who isn't her husband, though she'd never say that. She worries about him driving an hour home to Halcyon after twelve hours awake. She texts him 'home?' at 7:15 and he always answers with a thumbs-up.

relationships.name: Pete Iniguez
relationships.history: Pete joined day watch in the fall of 2025 on interior hall patrol. Within a month he was calling her 'Mom' over the radio, and she shut that down. In November 2025 she found the Hall C2 loading door propped with a trash can and Pete twenty minutes away in the cafeteria. She wrote it up exactly as it happened, and he got a verbal from Wren. Afterward, in the security office, he told her she was 'playing hall monitor for a paycheck,' and she raised her voice at work for the first time in years. Now they're polite on the radio and avoid each other everywhere else.
relationships.how_they_feel: She thinks he's lazy with the parts of the job that matter and charming with the parts that don't. She also knows his wife works county road crew and they're stretched thin, which makes her angrier at him rather than softer, because she thinks he should know better. She doesn't trust any door he says he checked.

relationships.name: Malik Dominguez
relationships.history: Malik and his family moved onto Yucca Street around the time he started at Vira at the end of 2025. He works Crew D nights in facilities, the same trade as Trent. Noor met him at 2:45 on a weekday afternoon, him just waking up and her just home, both of them out in their driveways glaring at the same broken sprinkler line between the yards. They fixed it together with parts from the hardware store in Saltbrush while Isaac rang them up. His son Miles is sixteen and has been asking Isaac about trucks.
relationships.how_they_feel: She likes him and appreciates that he keeps hours as strange as hers. He's the one neighbor she can wave to at 5 in the morning when he's coming home and she's leaving. She worries a little that he and Trent will end up commiserating about wives.

relationships.name: Tess Mondragon
relationships.history: Tess lives two doors down and runs receiving at Hall A3. They were the first two people Noor knew at Vira, because Tess flagged her down on her second week on patrol to complain about a truck driver who kept leaving the receiving route. They've had a standing arrangement since 2023: when Noor's days off line up with a delivery Tess has to wait for at home, Noor signs for it, and Tess feeds Maya's fish when the Rojases go to Hesperia. Tess has two cats, both of whom have tried to move into Noor's garage.
relationships.how_they_feel: Easy, neighborly, not deep. Noor thinks Tess is lonely and makes a point of inviting her for dinner on holidays. Tess always brings store-bought pie and apologizes for it.

relationships.name: Hana Sato
relationships.history: Hana lives on the same street and is Trent's shift lead on Crew B. Noor knows her mostly through block barbecues and through Trent's complaints and compliments, about equal in number. Their kids overlap at the Saltbrush school, and Hana's Ezra is a year behind Maya.
relationships.how_they_feel: Cordial and a little careful, because Hana is her husband's boss and Noor doesn't want to be the wife who calls the supervisor. She admires how Hana manages three boys and a crew. Privately she thinks Hana schedules Trent heavy on overtime, and she has never said so.

relationships.name: Kim Rasmussen
relationships.history: Kim runs the camera wall in the security office and is the person on the other end of most of Noor's radio calls. She's the only one on day watch older than Noor, and they bonded over reading glasses in 2023.
relationships.how_they_feel: She trusts Kim's eyes completely. She has half a plan to bid for the camera wall when Kim retires, and she suspects Kim knows.

relationships.name: Felix Haskie
relationships.history: Felix works the gate lane at the lift arm and was already a fixture when Noor started. He's Wren's protege. He has a six-year-old, and he and Noor trade parenting horror stories at shift change.
relationships.how_they_feel: She likes him. He's polite to everyone and takes the job seriously. She thinks Wren is grooming him for sergeant someday and that he'll be good at it.

wants: A standing date night with Trent that neither of their schedules can eat
Her mother to move closer, which will never happen
To sit down at work by 58
worries: That her marriage has become a scheduling problem
Her right knee, which clicks on stairs and swells after the fence walk
Money if Isaac enlists and they lose the help with Maya's mornings
Getting older than everyone else on the crew
secrets: She sometimes sits in her SUV in the driveway for ten minutes after work before going inside, just to be alone, the same way she did after the 2003 call
She turned down the chance to put in for sergeant in 2023 partly because she didn't want the job to own her evenings while Maya was five. She tells people it was because she was too new.
She has a savings account Trent knows about but has never looked at, which she calls her 'leaving money.' She has no plan to leave. Her mother told her every woman should have one.
inner_life.regrets: That she worked overnights through most of Isaac's early childhood and can't remember his first steps because she was asleep. She's determined not to miss Maya's, and with Maya she knows she's sometimes overdoing it.

health_and_money.health: Generally strong for 53. She walks eight to twelve miles a shift. Her right knee has early arthritis and she takes ibuprofen most days. Her blood pressure is borderline and her doctor in Halcyon wants her to cut salt, which she won't. She had a hysterectomy in 2021. She sleeps badly when Trent works and well when he's home, and hasn't told him that.
health_and_money.money: Better than it's ever been and still tight. Two Vira paychecks, a mortgage on Yucca Street that's less than the Victorville rent was, his sedan paid off, her SUV with two years left. They're paying down about eight thousand on a card from the move. She puts $200 a month into her own account and $100 into a college fund for Maya. Ruben's child support for Isaac stopped at 18, not that it was reliable before.

beliefs.faith: Raised Maronite Catholic by her father, with Baptist relatives on her mother's side. The church in Saltbrush is not her kind of church, but she goes at Christmas and Easter anyway, and on her father's birthday she lights a candle for him at home. She prays more than she goes to church and doesn't think that's anybody's business.
beliefs.politics: Registered independent and cynical about all of it. Law-and-order on the things she's seen up close, softer than people expect on healthcare and immigration because of the ER and her father. She votes in every local election and almost never talks about national politics at work, because it's not worth the fight.

knowledge.about_vira: She knows the campus physically better than most of the engineers: every door number, every camera blind spot, which halls run hottest, where the substation fence sags, which part of the lot floods during the monsoon. She has a vague idea that the halls hold computers for big companies, she doesn't know whose, and she doesn't ask. She knows the place opened in 2019 and that the people who've been here since the start talk about the early days like a war.
knowledge.about_lyra: She has never heard the name Lyra. She thinks Vira runs on ordinary building automation. She has logged a handful of odd things over three years as equipment glitches: the pedestrian gate on the north lot unlatching by itself one afternoon in 2024, the irrigation by the operations building coming on at 1:10 in the afternoon in July, and a hall door whose badge reader went green while she was still reaching for it. She wrote each one up, sent a ticket to facilities and moved on.
knowledge.about_marcus: She knows him by sight as one of the staff who rides a motorcycle in from Saltbrush, because she logs the motorcycle in the lot. She's never had a conversation with him beyond a nod.
rumors_they_believe: That Vira is going to add another block of halls on the south side, because of the survey stakes past the solar field
That one of the night-shift guys sleeps in his car in the lot between shifts
That the substation fence was cut once in 2021 and it never made the news

memories.what: Jumping Kim Lomeli's dead sedan in the staff lot in near-freezing cold. He was shaking and apologizing, and she followed him all the way to the highway in her SUV with her hazards on until his engine stopped sputtering.

Wren calling her 'ma'am' eleven times during orientation at the gatehouse. On the twelfth she said, 'Sergeant, I'm going to need you to pick a different word,' and Felix Haskie laughed so hard at the lift arm that he had to turn around.

Finding the Hall C2 loading door propped with a trash can, timing exactly how long it stood open, and then raising her voice at Pete Iniguez in the security office while Kim Rasmussen pretended to watch the cameras.

Trent's first day at Vira. They drove in together for once, in her SUV, and she dropped him at the gatehouse to pick up his badge like it was the first day of school. She told him 'Don't embarrass me,' and he kissed her through the window in front of the whole gatehouse.

Tess Mondragon flagging her down on the receiving route to complain about a delivery driver who kept wandering toward the cooling yard. They chased him down together in the patrol truck, and Tess invited her over for a beer that evening. It turned out they lived two doors apart.

Standing in her driveway in work boots next to Malik Dominguez in his pajama pants, both of them looking at a geyser from the busted sprinkler line between their yards, and fixing it with a part Isaac rang up at the hardware store.

The irrigation by the operations building coming on at 1:10 in the afternoon at 112 degrees. She logged it as a timer fault, and Kim Rasmussen confirmed on the camera wall that nobody was near the controller.

Isaac's graduation at the Saltbrush school. Hana Sato moved heaven and earth on the Crew B schedule so Trent could make it, and he and Noor sat together in the bleachers holding hands like teenagers for the first time in months.

conversation_starters: Ask her about the worst night on dispatch and she'll tell you about the best one instead
Ask which door on campus sticks in the heat and she'll name three, by number
Mention lentil soup and she'll ask who's sick
Ask how she and Trent manage the schedules and point at an imaginary whiteboard
Bring up the Navy and watch her jaw set
Ask her about her father's cooking
